key_insight: PathFM moves beyond predicting only marginal quantiles and instead models whole future trajectories, capturing how future values depend on each other over time. This makes forecasts more useful for path-dependent decisions like cumulative demand, peaks, and event timing.
problem_solved: Most time-series foundation models give accurate point or marginal forecasts but do not specify the joint dependence structure across the future trajectory. That leaves important trajectory-level quantities unresolved even when standard forecast scores look good.
method: Uses a trajectory-based forecasting formulation rather than independent marginal prediction.
Applies flow matching to generate coherent multivariate future paths.
Targets the full dependency structure of future trajectories so forecasts better reflect temporal and cross-variable interactions.
impact: For practitioners, this means forecasts can support downstream tasks that depend on the entire future path, not just each time step independently. It is especially useful in planning, risk analysis, operations, and any application where shape and timing matter.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of marginal forecasts vs. full trajectory forecasts
Flow matching pipeline diagram from history to future path generation
Multivariate time-series plot showing correlated future scenarios
Icons for cumulative demand, peak load, and event timing to show path-dependent use cases
paper_title: PathFM: Fast Generative Forecasting of Multivariate Trajectories
paper_authors: Jiachen Yao, Xiyuan Zhang, Annan Yu, Boran Han, Abdul Fatir Ansari
